title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles were stranded in San Francisco during Fourth of July celebrations because severe traffic gridlock drained their batteries while they sat motionless on city streets. At least a dozen vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, required intervention or towing. The system was deployed into conditions it was not designed to handle, where normal traffic flow assumptions broke down entirely due to holiday congestion and unexpected road closures.

The failure occurred in the planning and response layer of deployment, not in autonomous driving capability itself. Waymo had no mechanism to redirect vehicles away from areas it could not predict would become impassable, or to move them to charging stations as batteries depleted during extended idle periods. A human traffic management system monitoring the city's actual conditions during major events could have instructed the fleet to avoid or exit affected zones before battery depletion became critical.

A separate vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks on the road, though no injuries resulted. It is not established whether this represents a distinct failure or a consequence of the fleet being unable to navigate away from the congested area.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
# Summary

Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded in San Francisco during Fourth of July celebrations on Saturday, with their batteries draining while stuck in severe traffic following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up motionless on city streets, with some requiring towing. The company attributed the issue to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unexpected road closures that created unusual congestion. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks someone had set on the road, though no injuries were reported.

The incident prompted city officials to initiate discussions about preventing similar problems in the future. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie urged residents to be patient with traffic conditions and said his office would have conversations with public and private partners to improve the experience for future events. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen its system during major traffic disruptions. This incident follows an earlier December incident where Waymo vehicles experienced issues during a widespread power outage affecting over 100,000 customers in the city.
